agree.reason: The open apology, plain bad news and clear plan would ease a cold investor somewhat, but nothing commits to future updates or says when and how the company will raise before cash runs out, so a wary angel deciding on the next round is left uneasy.

honest.reason: The figures are accurate, but 7% against 13% is about 54% of the old rate, so 'nearly half as many missed appointments' overstates it slightly, and 'the rest of the business grew' hides that 3 other clinics also left.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out runway of about 11 months, that the chain was about 13% of revenue, and roughly 15% growth from the rest of the business, which recasts flat MRR in its best true form; it gives no figure for how many reminder customers would change the picture.

right_comparison.reason: Comparing flat MRR with what would have been a drop, and giving the current runway, fairly shows where things stand, but it never says what happens if nothing changes, such as how the 15% growth rate compares with the burn.

qualification.reason: The standalone launch and the threat from records systems come with no target, date or checkpoint the investor could use to judge whether the new approach is working.

objections.reason: It answers the missed updates and the lost customer head-on, but leaves out the obvious questions for an investor with the right to join the next round: when will you raise, will you cut burn, and will updates arrive on time from now on?

fit.reason: It is a well-structured investor update of about 400 words, under the 500-word limit, with a clear subject line and a specific request at the end.
